We are excited to announce the release of the next major version of Shoko Server! Shoko Server 6.0.0 is the biggest release we have made in years: the plugin system was rebuilt from the ground up, again, and this time almost everything the server does can be extended or replaced by a plugin. Hashing, release info, file relocation, metadata sources, images, orderings, airing schedules, scheduled actions, streaming and settings pages can now come from plugins. TMDB, the WebAOM renamer and the legacy Plex support moved out of the core and into plugins, the job queue was replaced with one built for Shoko, and every metadata source is now a first-class citizen. Note that **Shoko Desktop no longer works with the server**, since APIv1, which it relied on, was removed.

For our detailed report, we highly recommend reading the accompanying blog post.

[Read the blog post on our site](https://shokoanime.com/blog/shoko-version-6-0-0-released/)

[Read the changelog on our site](https://docs.shokoanime.com/changelog/shoko-server)

[Read the full changelog on GitHub](https://github.com/ShokoAnime/ShokoServer/compare/v5.3.3...v6.0.0)

> [!Important]
> **Before you upgrade:** (see the [Upgrading to Shoko 6](https://docs.shokoanime.com/getting-started/upgrading-to-shoko-6) guide for the full walkthrough)
>
> - **Web UI 2.6.0 ships with this release.** The 2.5.x Web UI only works with 5.x servers, so let the server install 2.6.0 if you manage the Web UI yourself.
> - **The first start after upgrading _may_ take a while.** Release info, images, every title and overview, and the TMDB data are moved into their new tables on that first start, which can take quite some time on large collections. Progress is shown while the server starts; let it finish, and back up your database before upgrading.
> - **Upgrades are only supported from 5.x.** If you're on an older version, upgrade to 5.3.3 first.
> - **Plugins need updating.** Plugins built for 5.x (`Shoko.Plugin.Abstractions`) or for an older major version of `Shoko.Abstractions` will not load. The server starts in failure mode and names them, so you can disable, update or remove them from the Web UI and restart. Plugin authors: see the new [Writing Plugins guide](https://docs.shokoanime.com/writing-plugins/) and the [migration guide from 5.x](https://docs.shokoanime.com/writing-plugins/migrating-from-5x).
> - **TMDB and WebAOM are now plugins.** Official builds include both. If you build Shoko yourself, or had either plugin disabled when you upgraded, install it from the plugin catalog (Settings → Plugin Management → Browse; both are in the Shoko Core Repository) and restart. Your existing TMDB links, metadata and artwork, and your WebAOM renamer settings, are kept either way; new TMDB artwork, like logos, is fetched as each show is refreshed.
> - **APIv1 is gone.** It had no authentication at all (see [Security](#security)), and Shoko Desktop relied on it, so Desktop no longer works with the server. APIv2 clients such as Shokodi keep working. For playing videos on your own computer, [Shoko Companion](https://github.com/ShokoAnime/Shoko.Companion) is in testing.
> - **Forgot your password?** Put a `password-reset.json` file in the data folder with the `username` and the new `password`, then start the server. It sets the password, deletes the file and shuts down; start it again and sign in. See [the FAQ](https://docs.shokoanime.com/faq#reset-your-password) for where the data folder is.
> - **The server now runs on .NET 10.** If you run the framework-dependent build, install the .NET 10 runtime first.
> - Your settings file is backed up to `SettingsBackup` in the data folder before it is migrated, so you can go back to 5.x if you need to.

## Security

- **Removed APIv1, which had no authentication.** Anyone who could reach a 5.x server could read and change its settings, manage users and their passwords, add and remove managed folders, and delete files, without signing in. If your 5.x server is reachable from outside your home network, upgrade or stop exposing it until you do. This is also why Shoko Desktop no longer works with the server. (642e5271af4d6e3b8e4a1285137548b4d18fcbd2) by @revam

- Fixed restricted users (users with hidden tags) being able to read and stream the files of series hidden from them by requesting the file by ID, hash, AniDB file ID or location ID. They now get a `403` on the file metadata and stream routes, stream sessions included, and such files are left out of listings and path searches. See [GHSA-xpwh-jh8w-7fhh](https://github.com/ShokoAnime/ShokoServer/security/advisories/GHSA-xpwh-jh8w-7fhh). A big thank you to @kats1123 for reporting it responsibly. Restricted users now also see a group that holds a series they may see, and unrecognized files are only shown to users without restricted tags. The list of every stored release is now admin-only; it let restricted users see the releases of hidden series in the 6.0 daily builds (see [GHSA-cw8p-qgw9-r8q5](https://github.com/ShokoAnime/ShokoServer/security/advisories/GHSA-cw8p-qgw9-r8q5), thanks again to @kats1123). ## Breaking Changes

- **.NET 10**: Moved the server, tray service, CLI and Docker images to .NET 10, and updated every dependency, with later NuGet package updates and a .NET 10 devcontainer. (#1441) (101351af137989b236f36253b3872cedacb1dccb, 22e1f3846859fae3422eb5e25dc49a715d64c837, 3878304ec2293eafb18ba42a0d2e0b63c50793eb, 82522dd6d31749e2fe7aa57197e93735e5d3a123, 619f27f45c4d694eb1871d7e3510bf78c734f3e2, 3d4e467ba1a0f57347d42cef9a45323f7fa41cc0, 090946f9be4d0578322c50ae42548ed8e2fd68e0, 74ebf76f9bf086fd8ed513bdea6cec45d2cb3c06) by @revam and @Foowy

- **New plugin abstraction**: Replaced the `Shoko.Plugin.Abstractions` NuGet package with the new `Shoko.Abstractions` package, with a new structure, new namespaces and a lot of new services. Plugins built for 5.x must be rebuilt, and most need changes. `IRenamer` and `IRenamerConfig` were replaced by `IRelocationProvider` and `IRelocationPreset` (see below). `IShokoEventHandler` is gone, but its events live on in the services that own them, so inject the service to keep listening: `IVideoService` (`VideoFileDetected`, `VideoFileHashed`, `VideoFileRelocated`, `VideoFileDeleted`), `IVideoReleaseService` (`ReleaseSaved`, `SearchCompleted`, …), `IVideoRelocationService` (`FileRelocated`), `IMetadataService` (`SeriesUpdated`, `EpisodeUpdated`, `MovieUpdated`, …), `IAnidbService` (`BanOccurred`, `BanExpired`), `IAnidbAvdumpService` (`AvdumpEvent`) and `IConfigurationService` (`Saved`). Plugin registration uses static abstract methods, `DataSource` became the `MetadataSource` registry, entries are named by a `MetadataGuid` (`anidb://series/1234`) instead of a number, and descriptions were renamed to overviews. Plugins built for the legacy package, or for an older major version of the new one, fail the start instead of being skipped. The upgrade copies the old `TMDB_*` tables into the shared metadata tables, giving the copied cast their characters, and moves the TMDB settings, the cast and network download switches included, into the plugin's own configuration. The APIv3 TMDB routes and models stay, now read from the shared tables, but TMDB's settings and actions moved to the plugin and `IsLocked` is gone from seasons. The renamer is now feature-frozen; use the Lua renamer or another relocation provider for anything beyond it. - **Legacy Plex support is now a plugin**: Moved the Plex client, the `/plex` routes, `/api/v3/Action/PlexSyncAll`, the watched-state sync and the "Plex Sync All" action into the bundled `Shoko.Plugin.LegacyPlex` plugin. Disabling the plugin turns it all off. (c48122f27ca0eeccec026ab5d94c1e61342f6d64, 4b2ce7e59286926c9ed64668d6447faff615a578) by @revam

  The legacy Plex support is kept for existing setups, but won't grow. For a modern Plex integration, keep an eye on [Shoko Relay](https://github.com/natyusha/ShokoRelay) by @natyusha, an upcoming community plugin that turns Shoko into a Plex Custom Metadata Provider (and more), succeeding the ShokoRelay.bundle agent. Plex [is removing the legacy agents system from new Plex Media Server releases in 2026](https://forums.plex.tv/t/announcement-custom-metadata-providers/934384), which the old Python-based bundles like ShokoRelay.bundle depend on, in favour of HTTP-based Custom Metadata Providers (PMS 1.43.0+). A provider has to be a web service Plex can reach, so it lives best inside Shoko as a plugin, and since providers can't hook into Plex's scanner the way the old bundles did, Shoko Relay builds a virtual file system to keep any folder layout working.

- **Removed APIv1**, along with the code only it used: change tracking, the legacy playlists, the `PlayedCount`/`StoppedCount` user data columns and the legacy `CL_ServerSettings` model. The `/Stream` routes legacy clients use moved into APIv2, while the `/Stream/Filename/{base64filename}/…` routes, which streamed a file by its path, were removed. If someone wants to take up the torch as a community plugin, the new plugin system has everything it needs. Just before the removal, the integration got better handling of revoked or expired tokens. Dev.releaseNotes:
`feat` (`abstractions`): **Expose the season calendar's bounds**:

- Added two `IAiringCalendarService.GetSeasonBounds` overloads returning `SeasonBounds`: the season a day falls in, and a given season
- With a type, a season starts by that type's lead-in, as the calendar files entries; without one, it is the calendar quarter

`chore` (`abstractions`): **Bump abstractions version to v6.0.0-alpha.144**.

`fix`: **Keep a series' cached air and end dates whole across threads**:

- `AnimeSeries.AirDate` and `EndDate` cached a `PartialDateOnly?` in plain fields; the struct is too large to be written in one step, so a concurrent first read could see it half-written and `ToDateOnly` threw
- The cached dates are now published through a box, so a reader sees all of a date or none

`fix` (`db`): **Index `AniDB_Anime_Staff` by anime**.

`fix`: **Register the plugins' web UIs after an earlier read of the web UIs**:

- A read of the web UIs before the plugins handed in theirs kept a list of the server's own alone, and the plugins' web UIs were then never registered
- Answered such a read without keeping it, registered the plugins' web UIs whatever was read before, and worked out what is served again once they are in

`fix` (`api`): **Make the release list admin-only**:

- `GET /api/v3/ReleaseInfo/Release` listed every stored release to any signed-in user, so a user with restricted tags could read the releases of series hidden from them
- Limited the route to administrators, as the other routes listing the whole release store are

`fix`: **Answer a transform's refusal to start a stream as the refusal**:

- The stream start endpoints answered every `StreamResourceException` from `GetRenditionAsync` with a 500
- Answered it through `StreamRenditionResponses.Refused` (400, 404 or 503), as a running session's resources already are
- Treated a refusal while restoring a session as the session being gone

`fix`: **Move links to directories on Windows**:

- `MoveFile` moved a link to a directory with `File.Move`, which finds no file there on Windows
- Moved and replaced such links as the directory entries they are, never what they point to

`fix`: **Leave movie markers and leading punctuation out of sort names**:

- `ToSortName` folded the accents of Latin letters and full-width forms
- Skipped leading punctuation (not symbols), a leading "Gekijouban" in any spelling or `劇場版`, then an article, each only when more title follows
- Matched the skipped words ignoring case

Closes #33

`feat` (`abstractions`): **Treat symbolic links to directories as links in listings and moves**:

- `FileSystemEntry` takes `bool? isDirectory`; `null` reads `IsDirectory` through `Stat` on first access
- Listings stat through a link up front only when following links, listing one kind, or leaving out a kind of link
- On Unix, `MoveFile` moves a link at either end with `rename(2)`, so a link to a directory is neither "not found" nor followed; another volume makes the link anew beside the destination and renames it over
- `SymbolicLinkStat.TargetStat`: what the link points to, one step and without following, read on first access

`fix` (`plugin`): **Check a dependency only against what the plugin takes from it**:

- A dependency's own copy of a third plugin's contracts no longer counts when the plugin's load context takes them from another dependency first, exporting or earlier in its order
- Applies to optional dependencies at the scan and to required ones after it

`refactor` (`abstractions`): **Take `ManagedFolderScanOptions` in the scan methods**:

- `ScanManagedFolder`, `ScheduleScanForManagedFolder` and `ScheduleScanForManagedFolders` take a `ManagedFolderScanOptions` instead of their loose arguments
- `ScheduleScanForManagedFolders` now also takes `CheckFileSize`

`fix`: **Hash another name of a known file only once**:

- Hashing a new file first takes the video it is another name of (a hard link, or a symbolic link to a known location), reading nothing when every enabled hash is known and none was forced
- Two locations of one file on disk hashed at once share one read (`TryHashOnce`)

`feat`: **Group linked locations of a video and count duplicates by group**:

- Locations that are the same file (hard links, symbolic links with their file) are stored as one file group: `PrimaryLocationID` (own ID for a primary; `IVideoFile.PrimaryFileID`), `IsSymbolicLink`, `SymbolicLinkTarget`; kept up to date on detection, hashing, relocation, `NotifyVideoFileChangeDetected` and folder scans (`ManagedFolderScanOptions.RepairGroups`), and handed on when a primary is removed
- `Import.GroupLinkedFiles` (on by default) groups them; a location can be kept (`IVideoFile.IsKept`, `IVideoService.SetVideoFileKept`)
- Import de-duplication, `IVideoService.GetVideosWithDuplicates` and the `/api/v3/DuplicateFiles` routes count file groups (`VideoFileGroup`, `GetVideoFileGroups`) and only remove whole groups that are not preferred, so links are never left broken
- `File.Location` gives `IsKept`, `PrimaryID`, `IsPreferredGroup`, `IsSymbolicLink` and `SymbolicLinkTarget`, and with `includeStat` `IsBrokenLink` and the link's own `LinkStat` (also `IVideoFile.LinkStat`); `PUT /api/v3/File/Location/{locationID}/Keep` sets the flag
- Added the file group columns to `VideoLocal_Place`, filled for videos with more than one location on upgrade

`feat` (`relocation`): **Optionally replace the same video at the destination**:

- `ReplaceSameVideoAtDestination` (setting, preset manager, requests, APIv3 relocation settings, body and query; off by default) lets a relocation onto another copy of the same video go ahead
- A symbolic link there to the file is replaced by it; otherwise the moved file is removed after a size check

`chore` (`abstractions`): **Bump abstractions version to v6.0.0-alpha.142**.

`fix` (`db`): **Read empty user tags as no tags**:

- `StringListConverter` drops empty entries, so an empty `UserTags` column reads as `[]` rather than `[""]`

`feat`: **Add episode kinds, source default orderings and ordering numbers**:

- Added `ExtraType` and `EpisodeCanonicity` to episodes, kept in the episode's extras
- Added `AbsoluteEpisodeNumber` per place, with `AbsoluteNumbering` on the ordering
- Kept the source's episode numbers per ordering entry; a shared number is a combined entry
- Added `IsSourceDefault`, `SourceDefaultCountries` and `GetSourceDefaultOrdering`
- Documented storing an alternative ordering for providers

`feat` (`abstractions`): **List several directories in one call**:

- Added `MaxDegreeOfParallelism` to `FileSystemListingOptions`
- Added `GetFileSystemEntriesByDirectory`, `GetFileEntriesByDirectory` and `GetDirectoryEntriesByDirectory`, walked in one parallel pool

`chore` (`abstractions`): **Bump abstractions version to v6.0.0-alpha.143**.

`feat` (`api`): **Give API tokens a stable ID, a creation time and a last-use time**:

- `ApiToken` gained `ID`, `CreatedAt` and `LastUsedAt`, as init properties so its constructor is unchanged
- A token's use is written at most once per five minutes, from the authentication handler
- APIv3 lists the ID and times, and revokes a token by its ID at `DELETE /api/v3/Auth/Token/{tokenID}`
- Added the `CreatedAt` and `LastUsedAt` columns to `AuthTokens`

`chore` (`abstractions`): **Bump abstractions version to v6.0.0-alpha.141**.

`fix` (`api`): **Settle the served APIs only once the web UIs are known**:

- Registering the controllers as services asked for them while the web host was built, which settled the APIs from the settings before any web UI could ask for one
- Before they are settled, every core controller is found and nothing is settled; a plugin reading `RunningApis` meanwhile gets what the settings say

`refactor` (`api`): **Turn the core APIs on and off without a restart**:

- A saved change to `EnableAPIv2`/`EnableAPIv3` applies at once: `ServedApis.Change` raises `Changed`, and `ServedApisChangeProvider` has MVC rebuild its routes
- The core's Swagger documents and the Swagger UI's list follow the APIs served
- `SHOKO_API_V2_ENABLED`/`SHOKO_API_V3_ENABLED` set the APIs at each start but may be overridden while the server runs
- Removed `ISystemService.ApisOnNextStart`, `CoreApiChangeRefusal.SetByEnvironment` and the web UI pick's refusal of an API an environment variable turned off

`feat` (`abstractions`): **List directories without a stat per entry, and say when a listing fails**:

- On Linux and macOS each entry's kind comes from `readdir_r`'s `d_type`, with a stat only through links and an lstat only where the file system gives no kind; no existence check before a listing
- `FileSystemListingOptions.ThrowOnError` throws for a missing or unreadable directory instead of leaving it out
- `IFileSystem.ReadSymbolicLink` reads a link's target as stored
